query: What safe, validated 13C-CH4 delivery methods for rodents (whole-chamber dosing, bolus dissolved CH4) minimize risk and what are realistic limits of detection for 13C in microbial and host metabolites by GC-MS/IRMS/LC-MS?

response.query: What safe, validated 13C-CH4 delivery methods for rodents (whole-chamber dosing, bolus dissolved CH4) minimize risk and what are realistic limits of detection for 13C in microbial and host metabolites by GC-MS/IRMS/LC-MS?
response.answer: Safe 13C-CH4 delivery methods for rodents include whole-chamber dosing and bolus administration. GC-MS/IRMS/LC-MS can detect 13C in microbial and host metabolites at parts-per-million levels. Detection limits are typically in the nanomolar range.

results.title: Recent Advances in the Detection of Food Toxins Using Mass ...
results.content: Recent technological advancements, such as high-resolution MS and tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS), have significantly improved sensitivity, enabling the detection of food toxins at ultralow levels. This review discusses the application of MS in detecting various food toxins including mycotoxins, marine biotoxins, and plant-derived toxins. (39);) In contrast, significant advancements in analytical techniques have revolutionized the field of food safety, and one such breakthrough is the application of mass spectrometry (MS) for the rapid and sensitive detection of food toxins. Recent advances and innovations in instrumentation, such as the development of high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) and tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS), have significantly improved sensitivity and selectivity, allowing for the detection of food toxins at ultralow levels. Mass spectrometry (MS) is a powerful analytical technique used to detect and quantify various compounds including food toxins. A rapid method based on ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) was developed for the simultaneous determination of 37 mycotoxins having various physicochemical properties in grain and animal feed samples.
